fields.meta_title: Anesthesia Consent Form Builder for Care Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an anesthesia consent form that names the plan and provider, asks pre-anesthesia questions and keeps its own signature.
fields.h1: Build an Anesthesia Consent Form for Every Anesthetic Plan
fields.hero_description: Describe how your anesthesia team works. Emergent builds an anesthesia consent form that records the plan and provider, and sends each pre-op answer to the provider.
fields.features_subheading: The plan, the person giving it and the answers that change how a case starts.
fields.feature_1:
General, regional, sedation or MAC

Offer each anesthetic your group uses as a choice the anesthesia provider marks. The patient then reads only the risks and alternatives your team wrote for the plan that was marked.
fields.feature_2:
A signature apart from the surgeon's

Place the anesthesia section after the surgical consent in one link, with its own signature and time. Show the person giving the anesthetic and the one supervising above that line.
fields.feature_3:
Fasting times checked against your rule

Ask when the patient last ate and last drank on the morning of the case. An answer inside your group's cutoff holds the case and alerts the provider who will give the anesthetic.
fields.feature_4:
Teeth and airway questions up front

Ask about dentures, bridges, loose teeth and how wide the patient can open their mouth. Each yes puts the patient on the provider's pre-op list with the details they typed.
fields.feature_5:
Past reactions and family history

Ask about the patient's own reactions to anesthesia and any blood relative's, like a fever in surgery. A yes reaches the anesthesiologist before surgery day, in the patient's words.
fields.feature_6:
Source code your developers can extend

Export the full code to your GitHub repository. Your team can run the anesthesia consent inside your scheduling system or patient portal and keep changing it there without a rebuild.

fields.tab_content_1:
Its own signature, for the anesthesia plan only

Harbor Anesthesia Partners puts its consent right after the surgeon's, in the same link. Dr. Priya Nair marks monitored anesthesia care for Mark Delaney's carpal tunnel release, given by CRNA Tom Becker under her supervision. Mark reads the risks for that plan and signs the anesthesia section at 6:52 a.m.
fields.tab_content_2:
One late breakfast holds a 9:00 case

Lumen Endoscopy Center's rule, set with its anesthesia group, is no solid food for 8 hours before sedation. Each morning check-in asks when the patient last ate. Greg Holloway types toast at 6:40 a.m. for his 9:00 a.m. colonoscopy. His case waits, and CRNA Joy Park sees the answer before anyone starts an IV.
fields.tab_content_3:
Four patients with loose teeth or bridges, listed first

Brightwater Oral Surgery sedates most of its wisdom tooth patients. Its anesthesia questions cover dentures, bridges, loose teeth and opening the mouth wide. This week 4 of 19 sedation patients answered yes to one. Their names top Dr. Hana Lee's pre-op list, each with the tooth or appliance they described.
fields.tab_content_4:
Before the hernia repair, a call about his uncle

Maple Hill Hospital's pre-op clinic asks if any blood relative has had a problem with anesthesia, like a high fever. Paul Reyes checks yes: his uncle ran a high fever during an operation in 2019. Dr. Omar Haddad, the anesthesiologist, gets the answer and calls Paul 2 days before his hernia repair.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Anesthesia Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Decide on the plans and the questions first. Emergent handles the build once those are written down.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pull the consent you sign today
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List the plans your group offers
fields.howto_step_1_des: Gather the consent your group uses now, whether it is a page in the surgeon's packet or a separate sheet. Mark every statement that belongs to anesthesia, not to the operation, since those move into a section with its own signature.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down each anesthetic your group gives, including monitored anesthesia care and any combination you use. For each plan, write the risks and the alternatives in the words your anesthesiologists use when they talk to patients.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Under the hospital Conditions of Participation, anesthesia is given by an anesthesiologist, another qualified physician, dentist or podiatrist, or a CRNA or anesthesiologist's assistant under supervision. Add one field for the person giving it and one for the supervisor.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Cover fasting times and any dentures or loose teeth. Add past reactions and family history: malignant hyperthermia is inherited and set off by some anesthetic gases and the drug succinylcholine.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your plans and questions into Emergent. It builds the anesthesia section with its own signature, plus a morning check-in for fasting answers. Change anything by asking, for example a version in Spanish or a guardian line for patients under 18.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Route each answer to its provider
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect the form to your scheduling system through its API. Fasting answers inside your cutoff hold the case on the schedule, and a yes on family history alerts the anesthesiologist by email or Slack before the day of surgery.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it, then have it reviewed
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run test patients through every plan and every yes answer, and check who receives each alert. Have your anesthesia leadership and a healthcare attorney review the wording before the first patient signs it.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is anesthesia groups' and hospitals' printable consents (AANA, UPMC, UTMB, a sedation dentist, two veterinary forms) plus one article on consent as a conversation. Each is a checkbox list of anesthesia types. None asks the pre-anesthesia questions or shows where the answers go. This page builds the anesthesia section as its own record: the plan picked from general, regional, sedation or monitored anesthesia care, the person giving it, the fasting, airway and family-history answers routed to that person, and a signature apart from the surgeon's.

At Maple Hill Hospital's pre-op clinic a patient says his uncle ran a high fever during a 2019 operation, and anesthesiologist Dr. Omar Haddad gets the answer and calls him 2 days before his hernia repair.

claims_to_source: Under the hospital Conditions of Participation, anesthesia may be given only by a qualified anesthesiologist, another MD or DO, a qualified dentist, oral surgeon or podiatrist, a CRNA under supervision, or an anesthesiologist's assistant under an anesthesiologist's supervision (42 CFR 482.52(a))
A pre-anesthesia evaluation must be completed and documented within 48 hours before surgery by someone qualified to give anesthesia (42 CFR 482.52(b)(1))
Hospital Conditions of Participation require a properly executed informed consent form in the chart before surgery, except in emergencies (42 CFR 482.51(b)(2))
Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited disorder triggered by volatile anesthetic gases and the drug succinylcholine

ANZCA expects anesthesia consent to be a process separate from surgical consent, with separate signatures or acknowledgment even on a single form, and a signature without the discussion is not acceptable consent
Valid informed consent needs capacity, disclosure and voluntariness
Consent discussions and signatures should come before the patient receives medication that could alter mental status
AANA lists obtaining informed consent for anesthesia among a CRNA's preoperative responsibilities
Consent can be express, given in words or in writing, or implied by actions
